crates/r2engine/src/program/info.rs:271-285: promoted slots are declared with CTypeLike::machine_bits. A promoted DWARF local would lose its declared type (double, pointer) under A1 unless the type is attached.
crates/r2ssa/src/strided.rs:180 debug_assert in meet; crates/r2ssa/src/constant.rs:37-42 is_value_preserving includes IntZExt.
findings.owner_crate: r2ssa (promote.rs: which slots are private scalars; graph.rs: one same-width copy congruence used by predicates.rs and values.rs); r2abi (argument registers of the convention); r2types (declared type of promoted storage by entry offset); r2dec (names and bindings of promoted storage)
findings.proposed_fix: Invariant: which store a read of a private scalar slot sees is decided once, by SSA construction, from the bytes alone, identically in every pass. Branch facts hold for every same-width copy of the compared value. A1 (agree, with corrections): (i) The promotion predicate is frame discipline, no escape, single width, and no overlap. If a declared object covers the place, it must also satisfy declared extent == place extent. That is an aggregate guard: a struct or array local accessed at constant offsets stays memory, otherwise A1 would split it into unrelated scalars (fake stack slots). It is a DWARF extent fact, not a name. (ii) The predicate does not depend on the declaration's role or its coordinate base, so pass 1 and pass 2 promote identically. (iii) The declared name AND the declared type attach to promoted storage by (entry-frame offset, width). r2types reads the type through info.rs locals; r2dec names the storage. Otherwise -O0 types regress to machine_bits. (iv) Where a declared object contains an escaped place, the escape covers that object's extent. The current 'this place and everything above it' rule (promote.rs:827) applies only without DWARF. (v) The home role predicate becomes 'register is a convention argument register (r2abi) AND not written earlier in the entry block'. That is a conjunction, and the return register is excluded. After A1 this role only drives naming. (vi) SsaGraph owns `copy_class(ValueId) -> ValueId`: follow Copy and same-size Cast only, computed once in O(V) with memoised chain walks (each SSA value has one def, so chains form a forest). predicates.rs uses it instead of the SSAVar-keyed collect_compare_copy_sources and canonical_compare_operand. values.rs uses it for both assume() insertion and narrow_where_defined lookup. constant::root_of stays as the separate numeric relation, defined as the ZExt-closure of copy_class. A2 (memory-SSA-fed Load values) is complementary and later.
findings.test: (1) The engineer's r2ssa function test mirroring the classify -O0 IL: one read at 0x2018, count 8, case(k) == k, and the selector's copy_class is the entry edi. (2) values unit: v = Copy(x) defined before `if (x <u 8)`, and w = v*4 in the guarded block gives stride 4 and [0,28]. (3) promote unit: entry block `xmm0 = xmm0 ^ xmm0; store [fp-8] <- xmm0_lo` with xmm0 as the return carrier is NOT a home. Old code: home. (4) promote unit: a declared 8-byte struct at fp-16 accessed as two 4-byte fields stays memory, while a declared 4-byte int accessed whole is promoted. (5) Engine trace test: the promoted slot set is equal in the first and final prepare for avg. (6) Behaviour: `pdd @ sym.classify` rv_O0g renders switch (x) with cases 0..5,7 and default -1; `pdd @ sym.avg` still declares `double s` and `int32_t i`.
findings.invariant: A must-alias, non-escaping, whole-object frame slot is an SSA variable whatever its name or role. The decision is a function of the bytes and declared extents only. held[copy_class(v)] applies to v.
findings.complexity: Promotion O(ops + places·log places), unchanged. copy_class O(V) once, O(1) lookups. Naming and type attach O(promoted·log declared).
findings.risks: Large -O0 rendering churn: binding plan, afv, obligation counts and r2r. The d549c6aa coalescing in r2types function_facts.rs becomes redundant and should be deleted, not kept alongside. The aggregate guard must use the rebased (SP) declared extents from the loader, never the first-pass FP ones.

findings.defect: F3 (confirmed, widened). The selector-to-label inverse is one wrapping u64 fold. Biased-negative switches are refused. `sub reg, c` biased switches are labelled on the biased value. SExt in the index chain is conflated with the entry's signedness. Labels come from the first-pass graph while the selector comes from the final graph.
findings.root_cause: walk_index (indirect.rs:113-155) folds every step into one EntryTransform at 64 bits. (a) It loses modular width, so x+3 at 32 bits is folded as T+24+8x, and checked_sub at :329 refuses entries below T+24 (the engineer's analysis is correct). (b) index_operand (:230-242) crosses IntAdd but not IntSub. `sub edi,10` (lifted as IntSub) therefore stops the walk, and the switch is named on x-10 with labels 0..7 instead of on x with labels 10..17. (c) The same function computes both the target chain (entry to target) and the address chain (selector to address), and :147 sets `signed = true` for an IntSExt on either. That flag is the entry-signedness of EntryTransform::target. On the index chain it is meaningless and ignored, and values.rs has no IntSExt transfer (:339-389 falls to top), so a sign-extended index gives reach top. (d) Labels are computed on pass 1's graph and carried as numbers (native.rs:1771-1777 -> NativeSwitch.cases at :1963-1971 -> r2source native.rs:157-160 case_value). The selector is re-derived on the final graph (semantic/prefix.rs:49-54). Two derivations of one switch fact, and per F2(5) the passes do not even promote the same slots.
evidence: crates/r2ssa/src/indirect.rs:131-150 (single u64 accumulation; :147 sets signed on any SExt), :230-242 (no IntSub arm), :323-335 (checked_sub and is_multiple_of per entry).
crates/r2ssa/src/values.rs:339-389: no IntSExt arm.
crates/r2engine/src/native.rs:742-762 (labels from `first`), :1963-1971 (carried into the capture); crates/r2ssa/src/semantic/prefix.rs:49-54 (selector from the final graph).
crates/r2ssa/src/semantic/certificates/mod.rs:208-214: the guard certificate requires labels == 0..bound, so biased selectors without an exact inverse lose the guard certificate.
findings.owner_crate: r2ssa (indirect.rs index chain and labels; values.rs IntSExt transfer)
findings.proposed_fix: Invariant: case(k) is the preimage of entry k under the index chain, restricted to the selector's proven range. Selector and labels are computed together, on the final artifact. Represent the chain as typed steps with widths: Add(c,w), Sub(c,w), Mul(s,w), Shl(n,w), ZExt(from,to), SExt(from,to), Copy/Cast. Keep it separate from the target-chain EntryTransform, which keeps `signed`. The inverse runs per step in reverse: subtract or add c mod 2^w. Division by s must be exact; where Mul could wrap at width w (s·max > 2^w-1), there are up to gcd(s,2^w) preimages, and the proven selector range must select exactly one or the label is refused. ZExt inverts by a range check; SExt by a range check on the sign-extended half. Add an IntSExt transfer to values.rs: exact when the source range lies within one sign half, otherwise top. The engine hands r2ssa per-entry targets by entry index. r2ssa labels entries on the final artifact, so the labels and the selector come from one derivation. Two-level tables add a Lookup(base,size) step whose inverse is a preimage map built once from immutable bytes (needs F7).
findings.test: r2ssa unit: (a) (x+3)@32, zext, *8, +T, Load8, BranchInd, guarded by (x+3) <u 8 gives cases -3..4 (as u32 0xfffffffd..4) on selector x. Old code refuses. (b) (x-10)@32 via IntSub gives labels 10..17 on x. Old code gives 0..7 on x-10. (c) values: sext32->64 of [0,7] is [0,7]; of [0x7fffffff, 0x80000000] it is top. (d) Engine: the label set in the final artifact's switch fact equals the one computed from the final graph.
findings.invariant: For each entry k, case(k) = {x in R_sel : chain(x) = base + k·stride}, and |case(k)| is at most 1 or the label is refused. Selector and labels come from one graph.
findings.complexity: O(steps) per entry, O(d·steps) in total. A lookup step adds O(index-table bytes) once.
findings.risks: Signed rendering of labels must follow the compare's signedness fact in predicates. Moving label derivation into the final prepare changes the capture contract (NativeSwitch carries entry-index to target, not value to target).

findings.defect: F4 (confirmed). pdf and every analysis tier depend on the full prepare of the function. An analysis error removes the listing, a panic kills the process, and an OOM kills the session.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed: OpenProgram::function_listing starts with `let prepared = self.prepare(entry)?;` (program/requests.rs:153-156), and disassemble_function passes the error straight through (r2s/src/listing.rs:133-150). The only catch_unwind is in r2dec test code (codegen.rs:1455-1466, inside the tests starting at :1402). The release profile unwinds (Cargo.toml:58, panic = "unwind"), so catch_unwind is viable. The engineer is right that OOM can only be prevented algorithmically (F1).
evidence: crates/r2engine/src/program/requests.rs:153-166.
crates/r2s/src/listing.rs:133-150.
Cargo.toml:53-59 release panic = "unwind".
Reproduced: pdf @ sym.classify aborts; pd 20 @ sym.classify works.
findings.owner_crate: r2engine (program/requests.rs listing policy; native.rs isolation boundary)
findings.proposed_fix: Agree with the engineer's (1): list the walked body (F6's resolved body where it exists, otherwise the plain walk) and append '; analysis refused: {reason}'. Agree with (2): NativeRefusal::Panicked at the root memo derive and at prepared_callee. Caveats: (a) the fallback listing is a different body (no dispatch arms), so the residual line must say which dispatches are unresolved. (b) A caught panic must carry its location (a panic hook that stores Location), and CI must fail on any Panicked refusal in the fixture sweeps. That keeps isolation from turning into masking, which is the only reading of catch_unwind the AGENTS.md anti-hack rule allows. (c) The memo must never store a derive that unwound.
findings.test: Engine: a Program whose prepare returns NativeRefusal::Prepare makes function_listing return the walked lines plus the refusal line, not Err. Panic isolation: an injected panicking callee leaves the root rendered, with the callee listed as Unread(Panicked{location}). Sweep test: zero Panicked refusals over all fixtures.
findings.invariant: A refusal or panic in f affects only f's analysis-derived annotations. Listing bytes never depend on analysis succeeding.
findings.complexity: O(body) extra walk, on the failure path only.
findings.risks: AssertUnwindSafe around the memo and returns tables; poisoned mutexes are already recovered (query/memo.rs).

findings.defect: F5 (confirmed, with additions). Callee facts are rebuilt for every root: `pdd @ main` rebuilds 14 callees. afl's survey is not memoised. Callee facts come from a different body derivation (no dispatch) than the callee's own root analysis.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed: read_callees -> prepared_callee (native.rs:570-606, walk at :586 without dispatch) -> CalleeFacts::derive (lib.rs:1397-1425, which includes a full r2types analysis). The memo holds one analysis (query/memo.rs:29-34). surveyed() reruns discovery on every call (requests.rs:170-173, :239-274), while references are memoised (:180-190). The engineer's soundness note holds as far as checked: unresolved dispatch gives an empty preserved set (semantic/shared.rs:797-806), no body-proven return (lib.rs:1359-1363), and unknown effects when obligations are incomplete (interproc/mod.rs:2231-2266). Addition: interfaces (parameters) recovered from a callee body cut at its dispatch miss any parameter used only in the switch arms. That is under-arity at call sites, which is wrong C, not just imprecise C.

crates/r2engine/src/lib.rs:1373-1425.
crates/r2engine/src/program/requests.rs:170-173, :239-274; mod.rs:478-485 (the revision covers bytes, names and entries).

findings.proposed_fix: Agree: a per-revision CalleeFacts table and a memoised Survey. Additions: (a) Invalidation must use the full Revision (bytes, names, entries), not only Moved. declaration_for reads prototypes by name (native.rs:590), so a rename or type change must invalidate. (b) Each callee derive needs its own Recording, so its Consulted ranges are its own. Today one Recording spans the whole root analysis (program/mod.rs:414-431). (c) Derive CalleeFacts from F6's single resolved body per function instead of adding a third walk variant.
findings.test: Memo stats: `pdd @ main; pdd @ sym.add` gives callee_hits > 0 and no second build@0x11a9. Sweep: SSA builds <= 2·functions. `afl; afl` runs one survey. Rename test: `afn` on a callee invalidates its CalleeFacts.
findings.invariant: Each function's callee facts are derived at most once per Revision, from the same resolved body as its root analysis.
findings.complexity: O(log N) lookup; a sweep costs O(N + C) preparations instead of O(N + E).
findings.risks: Stale summaries if invalidation misses names or entries revisions. Callees with jump tables now get their full bodies, so their interfaces change (more precise).

findings.defect: F6 (NEW, missed). Dispatch resolution runs one round, on the root only, over a partial body. That can silently under-approximate a switch: missing arms with no residual. Nested switches are never resolved. Every other consumer (low tier, discovery/afl, references/axt, callee facts) walks without dispatch, so a function's body has five derivations.
findings.root_cause: analyse() calls pointer_tables(&first) exactly once (native.rs:742) on a body walked with no dispatch arms. The final artifact is prepared with those tables (native.rs:746-762, :795) and nothing re-derives them. In round 1 the unresolved BranchInd has no successors (body.rs:513-516 stop, :658-663). The value analysis therefore sees no path from any arm back into the function. A loop-carried selector (a state machine `st = argc>1; for(;;) switch(st) { case 0: st = 2; ... }`) has a round-1 range ({0,1}) narrower than its real range. That passes indirect.rs's stride check, all entries decode, and the table is accepted with 2 targets. Arms 2..N are never walked and no refusal is recorded. The certificate at certificates/mod.rs:208-214 only drops the guard; it does not restore the arms. A dispatch that is reachable only through another table's arms is never resolved either. Separately, lift_body is called with an empty dispatch map by native::lifted (native.rs:148), discovery (program/returns.rs:99), references (program/requests.rs:210) and callee prep (native.rs:586 via walk). So afl on a stripped binary misses functions called only from switch arms, axt misses xrefs from arms, and callee interfaces miss parameters used only in arms. This contradicts discovery's own contract ('closed under walk it and take where it transfers', discovery.rs:9-12).
evidence: crates/r2engine/src/native.rs:742-762 (a single pointer_tables call), :795 (final prepare reuses `tables`).
crates/r2ssa/src/body.rs:507-519, :655-663 (an unresolved dispatch has no successors).
crates/r2engine/src/native.rs:148, :586; crates/r2engine/src/program/returns.rs:99; crates/r2engine/src/program/requests.rs:210 (all use lift_body with an empty dispatch map).
crates/r2ssa/src/indirect.rs:304-319 accepts any strided reach whose stride equals the load size. Nothing checks that the body was closed.
Not reproduced on a binary: review.c has one non-nested switch whose selector is an argument. Inferred from the code.
findings.owner_crate: r2engine (one resolved-body derivation per function per Revision, used by every tier). r2ssa provides a dispatch-reads query that stops after the values phase.
findings.proposed_fix: Invariant: a function's body is the least D with D ⊇ F(body(D)). F resolves every dispatch on the walked body, with arms from D included, so the value analysis sees every path. Iterate D_{i+1} = D_i ∪ F(body(D_i)) from D_0 = ∅ until nothing changes. The sequence increases and is bounded by the finite set of code addresses, so it terminates. At the fixpoint, F is evaluated on a closed body, so every accepted table's targets over-approximate the real ones. Monotonicity of F is not required, because of the union. Rounds are at most 1 + (number of dispatches discovered late), typically 2. r2ssa exposes the read query without running the full semantic collection: SSA + prep + predicates + values, stopping MemoryPrefix after the 'values' phase (semantic/prefix.rs:44-57). r2engine memoises `resolved_body(entry)` per Revision and serves native::lifted, discovery, references, callee facts, the root analysis and the F4 fallback listing from it. Discovery pays for resolution only on bodies that contain an unresolved indirect branch.
findings.test: Engine unit with a synthetic body: a loop whose selector is phi(entry {0,1}, arm0 sets 2, arm1 sets 3), with a guarded 4-entry table. The resolved dispatch has 4 targets. Old code gives 2 targets and no refusal. Nested: a dispatch reachable only from arm 2 of another table is resolved. Discovery: a stripped fixture where f is called only from a switch arm lists f in afl, and axt f shows the arm. Old code misses both.
findings.invariant: Every resolved dispatch is validated on the closed body. One body per function per Revision, shared by all tiers.
findings.complexity: O(R·(prep+values)) per function with dispatches, R <= 1 + late dispatches (typically <= 2). Zero extra for functions with no indirect branch. Per-Revision memo O(log N).
findings.risks: Discovery becomes costlier on switch-heavy binaries (one values solve per such function). The returns fixpoint and discovery must consume the same resolved bodies, or 'returns' is decided on a different body than the one listed.

findings.defect: F7 (NEW, missed). Table targets are trusted from file bytes in memory that may be written (writable sections, or loader-relocated ranges). Target validity is 'some instruction decodes there' at any readable address, including data. On x86 almost anything decodes.
findings.root_cause: pointer_table (native.rs:1735-1790) reads file bytes through Program::read and checks only mapped length and decodes(target) (native.rs:2221-2230). decodes needs only a readable address and a successful lift. It never consults loader_writes (the Program trait has it, native.rs:66, and it is unused here), the write permission, or whether the target lies in code. The facts exist in r2image (Segment.permissions.write/execute, r2image lib.rs:59-62, :75-83), but the engine's Container Section has no write flag (program/source.rs:83-94). So rule 3 of AGENTS.md (facts arrive through Source) is not satisfied for this fact. A PIE absolute table in .data.rel.ro (R_*_RELATIVE) would be read as file addends, and a table in .data could be rewritten at runtime.
evidence: crates/r2engine/src/native.rs:1735-1790 (no loader_writes, no permission check), :2221-2230 (decodes only needs read + lift).
crates/r2engine/src/program/source.rs:83-110 (Section: name, vaddr, vsize, is_code, loaded; no writable).
crates/r2image/src/lib.rs:59-62, :75-83 (Permissions with write/execute on Segment).
No PT_GNU_RELRO handling anywhere (grep relro finds nothing in r2image or r2engine).
findings.owner_crate: r2image (permissions, RELRO, relocation-resolved reads) -> r2engine::program::Source/Container (projection) -> r2engine native.rs (policy)
findings.proposed_fix: Invariant: a table's bytes are the bytes the program reads at run time, in a range it cannot write after load. Every target lies in a container-stated code section. Project `writable` (and `executable`) into Container.sections. r2image states PT_GNU_RELRO ranges and offers read-as-loaded for relocated immutable ranges (RELATIVE gives base + addend). pointer_table accepts [base, base+span) only if it is non-writable, or RELRO read as loaded. Targets must satisfy Section::is_code. For BranchInd, a target inside an instruction the walk already decoded is a refusal (boundary conflict). Otherwise refuse with evidence naming which property failed.
findings.test: Engine unit: a table in a writable section is refused with 'writable'; a table in a loader-written range without RELRO is refused; with RELRO and a RELATIVE addend it is read as base+addend. A target in .rodata is refused although it decodes. r2image unit: an ELF with PT_GNU_RELRO states the range.
findings.invariant: Table bytes are immutable after load and read as loaded. Targets are in code.
findings.complexity: O(log sections) per range or target lookup.
findings.risks: Refusing writable tables may reduce resolution on binaries whose tables sit in .data (rare for compilers). Refusal is the correct outcome there.

findings.defect: F8 (NEW, precision). The table-read shape is narrower than the mathematics requires. Struct-array dispatch (`cmds[i].fn()`, stride 16 with 8-byte load), singleton reaches, computed branch tables without a load (ARM32 `addls pc, pc, r0, lsl #2`), and two-level tables are all refused or mis-named.
findings.root_cause: indirect.rs:311-318 requires stride == load size. The comment 'a read that steps by anything but what it reads leaves gaps, and neither is a table walk' is not a correctness condition: the read set {base + stride·k} of `size` bytes is well defined for any stride >= size. indirect.rs:304 needs stride() Some, and strided.rs:117-121 returns None for singletons, so a proven single target is refused. dispatch_load requires a Load (indirect.rs:266-270, :292-296), so a target whose own reach is a finite strided set of code addresses (ARM32 branch-of-branches, x86 computed `jmp base+16·i`) gets 'not a constant affine function of a load'. For two-level tables, index_operand returns None at a Load (:230-242), so the selector is table[c], not c. The doc at :195-196 claims the opposite ('names c').
evidence: crates/r2ssa/src/indirect.rs:195-196 (the doc claims a load names c), :230-242 (no Load arm), :266-270, :304-318.
crates/r2ssa/src/strided.rs:117-121.
findings.owner_crate: r2ssa (indirect.rs read model)
findings.proposed_fix: Generalise the read: reach R (a finite strided set, count >= 1) with load size s <= stride, and span = (count-1)·stride + s. Direct computed targets: when the BranchInd target's own reach is a finite strided set, that set is the target set, validated by F7's is_code check, with no memory read. Two-level tables: the Lookup step from F3.
findings.test: r2ssa unit: base + 16·i + 8 with i <u 4 and Load8 gives count 4, stride 16, size 8. A constant address with Load8 gives count 1. ARM32-shaped `pc = pc+8 + (r0<<2)` with r0 <=u 3 gives 4 direct targets.
findings.invariant: Every finite, immutable, code-valid target set the value analysis proves is resolved.
findings.complexity: Same as F1: O(d) per dispatch.
findings.risks: Stride > size opens more candidate reads, which F7's validity check must keep honest.

cross_cutting:
My objections to the engineer's report, and what I found alongside:
1) "Bounded is not proven" is the wrong diagnosis. [0, 2^32-1] for zext32(top) is a proven fact. The real rule is that a consumer inferring an EXTENT must intersect the index reach with an extent some other fact proves (the meet of two facts, not a cap). For tables that is the immutable section (F1/F7). For stack objects it is the frame. The places that should do this are semantic/shared.rs:1813, certificates/mod.rs:558 and certificates/stack.rs:1127. The proposed `ValueRanges::proven_bounds(value, carrier_width)` would need the domain to track where each bound came from. That is a heuristic, and so is F1's 'selector bounded only by its width' refusal, which throws away provable u8 and two-level tables. I reject both.
2) The copy-root unification has to name its equivalence. There are three relations today. constant::root_of follows Copy/New/Cast/IntZExt and so changes width. predicates.rs follows Copy only, keyed by SSAVar. DecompilePrepFacts::canonical_root closes over phis. Branch facts need same-width congruence; a numeric root that crosses ZExt makes StridedInterval::meet compare mismatched widths (debug_assert at strided.rs:180). shared.rs:1593-1594 already works around per-ValueId ranges with `upper_bound(v).or_else(upper_bound(root_of(v)))`. That call should go once copy_class exists.
3) Pass drift: prepare runs up to three times (native.rs:736, :757, :795) with different declarations. For avg, pass 1 has 2 declared slots and pass 2 has 5. Pass 2 also declares a Local at entry SP+0 extent 8, which is the return address (declared_slots.rs:118 trace). That comes from the restatement/rebase path (native.rs:769-795) and is wrong outside this cluster. Promotion, selector and labels must not depend on which pass is running.
4) spills_an_incoming_value: the engineer's diagnosis is incomplete. The OR with argument_carriers ignores earlier writes, and build.rs:145-162 passes the return register as an argument carrier. The same `abi_carriers` list serves two unrelated facts: the width of boundary carriers, and parameter homes.
5) Soundness hole missed by the report: single-round dispatch resolution on a partial body can under-approximate a loop-carried selector (F6). The fixpoint is required for correctness, not just for nested switches.
6) Table immutability and target validity (F7) are missing from the engine even though r2image has the facts. This is what really guards against fake switch arms on x86.
7) Domain gaps in values.rs that matter for decbench (out of this cluster's fixes, but they share one owner): no IntSExt transfer; no Load transfer even for immutable memory, where a read-only memory oracle would also type the rv_O2 CSWTCH table as an int array rather than the string "\n"; signed compares never narrow, although they are exact when both operand ranges lie in the same sign half (loop bounds, -O0 `for (int i...)`); no backward narrowing through Subpiece/SExt.
8) optimize.rs:111-115 says constants and folds 'run until neither moves', but DecompilePrepConfig caps max_iterations at 1 (optimize.rs:47-53). That is a cap contradicting its own stated fixpoint, and it is part of why the copy-root gap is observable.
9) Stale or misplaced docs: body.rs:8-11 ('a value domain that does not exist yet'); promote.rs:15-24 stacks the docs of resolved_stack_address and spills_an_incoming_value onto `unplaced`; indirect.rs:195-196 says a load 'names c' when the code does the opposite.
10) Suggested order: F7 (Container facts) -> F1 -> F3+F8 (read model, one rewrite of DispatchTableRead) -> F2 (A1 + copy_class) -> F6 (resolved-body fixpoint, which then serves F4 and F5) -> F4 -> F5.
open_questions: F2/A1: promote every whole-object private scalar slot, including DWARF locals and parameter homes, with declared name and type attached by entry offset and declared aggregates kept in memory. This accepts broad -O0 r2r churn and deletes the d549c6aa coalescing. Agreed?

Unguarded full-width selectors (u8 tables, two-level tables): accept when the range is immutable, the targets are in code and on instruction boundaries (F7), and the entries decode? I recommend yes. Or refuse as a residual?
RELRO: implement PT_GNU_RELRO plus read-as-loaded for RELATIVE relocations in r2image now, so PIE/ARM absolute tables in .data.rel.ro resolve? Or refuse loader-written tables for now?
F6: should discovery (afl) and references (axt) pay one values solve per function with an unresolved indirect branch, to close over switch arms? Without it, stripped binaries miss arm-only callees.
Panic isolation: is catch_unwind at the root memo and prepared_callee boundaries acceptable if every caught panic carries its location in the output and CI fails on any Panicked refusal?
The pass-2 declared Local at entry SP+0 (return address) for avg: file it as a separate stack/interface defect, or fold it into F2 since it feeds the promotion predicate?

label: critique:lowering
cluster: How r2dec lowers P-code to C, reviewed adversarially: shift and rotate definedness, partial-register entry reads and result width, the call-clobbered thread pointer, float load typing, lane dataflow, recovery of float-class interfaces, ARM and x86 flag idioms, and signedness and cast discipline. I verified every cited file:line against HEAD 5a6571fc and reproduced the outputs with target/debug/r2s.

findings.defect: rotl (rv_O0g and rv_O2) renders `x << t | x >> (uint8_t)(32 - t)` with t = r & 31. At t == 0 the second shift is `x >> 32`, which is UB in C. P-code gives 0 there and x86 `rol` gives x, yet the proof line still says 0 refused. Every non-literal INT_LEFT, INT_RIGHT and INT_SRIGHT has the same problem. The same unproven-operator gap also covers signed division: arm64 sparse_switch renders `(int32_t)W1_0 / (int32_t)W2_0` without proving that the case W1 == INT_MIN with W2 == -1 cannot happen. That case is defined on AArch64 SDIV (it yields INT_MIN) and is UB in C.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed. The origin is that no layer owns C operator admissibility. r2ssa records the machine semantics for overshift (Zero/SignFill), and the r2rewrite evaluator follows them. The typed boundary of Shift, however, fixes only the signedness of the shifted operand. Four r2dec renderers each spell a bare `<<`/`>>`. The proposer's invariant is also slightly wrong. The side condition is not count < width of the promoted operand. For a narrow left shift (W < 32) the operator is UB-free only when count < W, or when the operand is converted to unsigned int and count < 32. Right shifts are safe when count < the promoted width. The proposal to add a new term-level interval pass inside r2rewrite would create a second owner of ranges. r2ssa already solves this count: values.rs:342-363 has IntSub, IntAnd-with-constant and ZExt transfers, so uniq:0x63480 = 0x20 - (CL & 0x1f) is already [1,32] in ValueRanges. The missing piece is transport of that range, not a new domain. MachineOvershiftBehavior::MaskCount and ::Checked are never produced by lowering. They are dead variants that eval.rs:189 still matches.
evidence: reproduced: out/rv_O2.rotl.pdd `return EDI_0 << tmp_63380_1 | EDI_0 >> (uint8_t)(32 - tmp_63380_1);` with tmp = SIL_0 & 31, so the count lies in [1,32]

findings.owner_crate: r2ssa owns the count/operand range facts, which it already computes. r2rewrite owns the C operator admissibility decision in TypedBoundaries and the rotate rule. r2dec only spells, through one shared shift spelling instead of four.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Transport, not a new domain. In import.rs::declare_leaf_facts, add arena.declare_range(leaf, artifact.values().get(value)). In r2rewrite, count_range(term) is a memoised fold over TermKind that reuses r2ssa::StridedInterval's own add/sub/and_mask/zext/rem transfers. Leaves seed from the declared range, literals are exact, and anything else is top. For machine-expr nodes, read ValueRanges of the count's ValueId directly. (2) TypedBoundaries gains a per-node Admissibility result. For Shift: Operator when (kind == Left && W < 32) ? hi(count) < W : hi(count) < promoted_width. Otherwise Total, spelled with the prelude helper r2sleigh_{shl,lshr,ashr}_W(x, c), which has exact P-code semantics and evaluates each argument once. For signed Divide/Remainder: Operator when 0 ∉ range(divisor), and either INT_MIN ∉ range(dividend) or -1 ∉ range(divisor). Otherwise Total, spelled with a helper that has the architecture's P-code semantics. (3) Add the rule shift.rotate: Or, Xor or Add of Shl(x, t) and LShr(x, Sub(W, t')), matched with same_value(x, x') and same_value(t, t') and hi(count_range(t)) < W, plus the mirror for rotate-right. It rewrites to a new TermKind::Rotate{dir, value, count}. The eval proof covers t in [0, W) at 8/16/32/64. The measure drops by 3 nodes. Spell it r2sleigh_rotl_W, or inline as `(x << t) | (x >> (-t & (W-1)))`, which GCC and Clang both recognise as rol. This covers x86 ROL/ROR, AArch64 RORV (count masked with 31/63) and ARM32 ROR-by-register (count & 0xff: a range, not a mask). SHLD/SHRD need a funnel variant. (4) Replace the four r2dec sites with one spell_shift(kind, value, count, admissibility). Delete the dead MaskCount/Checked variants or give them a producer. The shift-count range is not special. It is the first instance of a general 'C side condition' fact: shift range, zero divisor, INT_MIN/-1, and narrow multiply. It belongs in TypedBoundaries as a per-node result that the proof line counts.
findings.test: Behaviour: compile the decompiled rotl (O0g and O2) with -fsanitize=shift,signed-integer-overflow -fno-sanitize-recover. Call it for r in {0, 1, 31, 32, 33} and compare with the original through an asm shim. The old output traps at r = 0 and r = 32. Unit: the typed boundary for Shift(LogicalRight, x32, Sub(32, And(r, 31))) is Total, for Shift(Left, x32, And(r, 31)) it is Operator, and for Shift(Left, x16, And(r, 31)) it is Total, because the count can reach 16 to 31 at W = 16. rule_proofs gets rotate templates built from occurrence-distinct leaves. Also compile the arm64 sparse_switch with (W1, W2) = (INT_MIN, -1) under UBSan against a qemu-aarch64 run of the original.
findings.complexity: Linear. count_range is O(|arena|) once, memoised per TermId, with O(1) per node for admissibility. The rotate rule is O(1) per Or node once same_value is O(1) (see the flag finding).
findings.invariant: A C operator is emitted only where its C side conditions are proven from r2ssa ranges: shift count, zero divisor, and INT_MIN/-1. Everywhere else the spelling is total and equal to the P-code semantics.
findings.risks: Leaf ranges must be keyed on the canonical occurrence. ValueRanges is flow-insensitive per value (function/mod.rs:1182-1188), which is sound in SSA. Helpers are less readable where proofs are weak. The rotate rule must not fire on ARM32 counts that are not reduced mod W.

findings.defect: rv_O2 sext renders `uint64_t RAX_0; RAX_0 = (RAX_0 & ~...) | (uint64_t)(uint16_t)(int8_t)DIL_0; return (uint32_t)RAX_0 - (uint32_t)(RAX_0 * 4);`. This reads an indeterminate C object, returns uint32_t where the source returns int16_t, and the proof line neither lists RAX_0 as held from entry nor refuses it. rv_O2 add gets uint64_t parameters from `lea eax,[rdi+rsi]`.
findings.root_cause: I confirm the three causes, with corrections. (a) deadphi.rs observed_input_bytes has no Insert arm, and Add/Sub/Mul/Neg/SExt/Or/Xor/shifts fall back to whole. Roots are seeded at the whole carrier width (dependency_closure, the line `let mask = width(value)`). The exact transfers are finer than 'prefix' suggests. Add, Sub, Mul, Neg and Shl-by-any-count, including a variable count, have a prefix closure. LShr and AShr by any count have a suffix closure, and AShr also reads the sign byte. SExt maps each output byte at or above the source width to the source's top byte. Or/Xor/Not are byte identities. Insert splits into window and outside at byte granularity, with both inputs feeding a partially covered byte when the position is not byte aligned. (b) Correction to the proposer. 'Result width = min(ZEXT width, first byte that may depend on an unspecified input)' is unsound as written. The closure is a may-dependence over-approximation. Over-approximating taint under-approximates the width, which silently drops result bytes (for example when garbage cancels, as in x - x on a partially written register). Narrowing needs either must-dependence or corroboration from the consumer side. The rv_O2 disassembly gives both. Callee side, EAX = RAX_1 - 4*RAX_1 = -3*RAX_1 mod 2^32 is a bijection in RAX_1, so byte 2 must depend on RAX_0's byte 2, but proving this needs the affine canonical form, not the byte closure. Caller side, main 0x11ed `movsx r8d, ax` observes only 2 bytes. (c) The r2dec hole is confirmed. entry_supplied_reads skips any symbol written anywhere (lib.rs:582), and the RAX_0/RAX_1 coalescing hides a read-before-write in the same statement. The deeper cause is that the certifier reasons over C symbols after coalescing, when it should key on SSA versions.
evidence: objdump rv_O2 sext 0x1564 `movsx ax,dil`, 0x1569 `lea edx,[rax*4]`, 0x1570 `sub eax,edx`: bits 16..31 of EAX depend on the entry value of RAX

findings.owner_crate: r2ssa owns one per-op byte dependency relation and derives three facts from it: backward demand, forward unspecified bytes, and parameter and result width. r2engine's interprocedural pass owns caller-observed result bytes and signedness, delivered through r2types. r2dec owns only the certification check, keyed on SSA facts.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) In r2ssa, define dep(op, out_byte) -> in_bytes once with the transfers listed in the root cause. Derive observed_input_bytes (backward) and a forward unspecified_bytes closure from it. Seed the forward closure from entry values of registers that the convention names neither as an argument slot nor as preserved, and from CallDefine values of non-result carriers. Seed the backward roots at the recovered result's observed width, not at the carrier width. Prove each transfer: flipping any input byte outside dep(M) never changes an output byte in M. Check this exhaustively at 8/16 bits and by z3 at 32/64. (b) Result width: take the max over returns of narrow(return value). narrow(v) is the smallest w such that every byte at or above w is proven zero, by ValueRanges or known bits rather than by syntactic ZExt, or must-depends on an unspecified input. Must-dependence holds when the byte is reached only through transfers that are bijective in that byte (Copy, Insert, ZExt, SExt, Subpiece, Piece, Add/Sub/Xor with an operand independent of that input, Mul by an odd constant after r2rewrite affine canonicalisation). Where only may-dependence holds, narrow only when the caller-observed bytes from r2engine (all call sites visible, address not escaped) agree. Otherwise keep the wide result and let (d) refuse. Signedness comes from caller evidence, for example movsx at every call site. (c) The machine projection narrows a value to its observed low run, once and upstream. INSERT(RAX_0, lane16, 0) observed at 2 bytes is then the lane, and RAX_0 is dead. (d) In r2dec, the certifier checks rendered reads of SSA version-0 values of non-parameter, non-preserved registers and of CallDefine values. Each is a visible refusal and never an uninitialised C object. Remove the flow-insensitive `written` excuse.
findings.test: Differential: an asm shim fills RAX with random garbage and then calls both the original sext and the compiled decompiled sext for all 256 inputs. The sign-extended low 16 bits must be equal. The old output depends on the garbage. Unit: dep() proof harness per op, flipping bytes outside the transfer. Unit: deadphi on INSERT(RAX_0, SEXT(DIL), 0) followed by *4 and a subtract, returned at 2 bytes, gives observed_bytes(RAX_0) == None. Negative unit: for `EAX = INSERT(RAX_0, x16, 0) - INSERT(RAX_0, x16, 0)`-style cancellation, may-taint alone must not narrow a 4-byte result. O2 `add` recovers two 32-bit parameters. The r2dec certifier refuses a synthetic read-before-first-write of an EntryValue binding that is coalesced with its own INSERT.
findings.complexity: Linear. Masks only grow (at most 9 states per value), so each closure is O(E·9). Must-dependence is the same walk restricted to bijective edges. Caller-observed bytes cost O(call sites) with the existing interprocedural pass.
findings.invariant: A rendered result never includes a byte that must depend on an ABI-unspecified input. Narrowing on may-dependence alone requires consumer corroboration. No rendered C reads a version-0 value of an unspecified register.
findings.risks: Variadic callees read AL. R10 is GCC's static chain. AArch64 x8 is the indirect-result register, which cc-arm-64.sdb.txt lists only as a clobber, so it must be modelled as an argument-class slot or sret functions will refuse. On Darwin x18 is reserved, on Linux it is a temporary. Results split across carriers (RDX:RAX) need per-carrier width.

findings.defect: rv_O0g and rv_O2 main declare `uint64_t FS_OFFSET_15;`, never assign it, and read it in the stack-canary check, while the proof line lists only FS_OFFSET_0. rv_O2 main also declares `uint64_t XMM0_4;` and reads it uninitialised as `r2sleigh_float_from_bits_64(XMM0_4)`, which is avg's result. That read is certified too.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed on both halves. The precision defect: SourceCallEffect is two-valued (clobbers = !preserves). radare2's cc sdb names no fs/gs base, so clobbered_by_a_call adds FS_OFFSET and rename emits a CallDefine after every call. The soundness defect, which is the real origin of the wrong C: r2dec treats CallClobbered as entry-declared and exempts it from definite assignment, so any read of a CallDefine value is printed as an uninitialised variable. The XMM0_4 case shows this is not specific to FS. The proposer missed an interaction. r2ssa already implements IPA-RA callee summaries (CalleePreservedCarriers, preserved_call_carriers), and rv_O2 main relies on them: `call avg; mov edi,5; call fact; cvttsd2si ebx,xmm0` keeps avg's xmm0 alive across `call fact`. A CallDefine read that remains after those summaries are applied has no evidence behind it, so refusing it is right. The summaries cannot cover imports (printf), so the thread pointer still needs an ABI fact.

findings.proposed_fix: (a) Make SourceCallEffect three-valued: Preserved | Clobbered | SystemReserved. SystemReserved is an ABI table with cited provenance. For SysV x86-64 (psABI Fig. 3.4): %fs base, 'reserved for system (thread-specific data)'. The same figure makes the MXCSR control bits and the x87 CW callee-saved, so the table should carry those too. i386 uses %gs. Win64 GS/TEB needs a decision. AArch64 TPIDR_EL0 needs a decision, and x18 depends on the OS. rename emits no CallDefine for SystemReserved. Mapping the name to storage (Sleigh FS_OFFSET against radare2's register name) belongs to r2sleigh-lift register naming. If the class goes into cc sdb (for example cc.amd64.reserved=...), raise an upstream radare2 PR. (b) In r2dec, remove CallClobbered from binding_is_entry_declared. A rendered read of a CallDefine value that is neither the callee's result nor preserved under an IPA-RA summary is a visible refusal. XMM0_4 then refuses until the float-class result finding makes avg's result a real call output.

After it, `double d = avg(...)` is carried across fact() through IPA-RA. Unit: for the amd64 SourceCallEffect, the class of FS_OFFSET is SystemReserved. The binding plan refuses a synthetic read of RCX's CallDefine after an unsummarised call.
findings.complexity: O(1) per call per register; the certification check is O(uses).
findings.invariant: Every value the rendered C reads is assigned on every path before the read, or is a parameter, or is a call result or a carrier the callee is proven to preserve. A call never redefines a register that the ABI reserves to the system.
findings.risks: Code that changes the FS base (arch_prctl or wrfsbase wrappers, green threads, libc TLS setup) is mis-modelled, so the class should be keyed per ABI and could be dropped where a lifted wrfsbase is observed in the body. MXCSR and x87 CW are only partially callee-saved (control bits, not status bits).

findings.defect: rv_O0g avg renders `double tmp_6b00_4 = r2sleigh_float_from_bits_64(v[i]);` with v declared `const double*`. The expression v[i] already has type double, so the output converts the value to uint64_t and then reinterprets the bits, which is wrong C.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed. The load statement claims its RHS type from a hint (type_hint_for_var(dst), falling back to uint_type_from_size(dst.size)). The access renderer, however, spells ParamArray as `base[index]` at the declared pointee and ignores elem_ty. The claimed type (uint64) and the actual type (const double) disagree, and convert() bridges them with float_from_bits. The term-level typed boundary makes the same mistake: Load/Subscript produce `own` and require ptr(own) instead of taking the pointee of the base's produced type. A second, latent cause: same_type and convert do not remove qualifiers, so a `const double` source matches the (_, Float) reinterpretation arm rather than (Float, Float). Both are symptoms of r2dec having four renderers that each state types (see cross_cutting).
evidence: reproduced: out/rv_O0g.avg.pdd `double tmp_6b00_4 = r2sleigh_float_from_bits_64(v[i]);`

findings.owner_crate: r2rewrite typed.rs owns the produced type of Load/Subscript. r2dec access_syntax returns (expr, CType) from one place and does not re-derive it.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept the proposer's fix, with one more requirement. The access spelling returns (expr, the CType it has), decided once. In typed.rs, the produced type of Load/Subscript is unqualified(pointee(produced(base))) when the widths agree and both are the same class. When the widths agree but the classes differ (a type-punned load), the produced type is the pointee and the reader's boundary spells the reinterpretation. convert and same_type work on unqualified types but keep volatile, which must never be removed from an access. Delete the hint-based elem_ty in the statement path. The statement path then assigns the typed expression, which it gets from the term or machine renderer.

Differential: for random arrays the compiled output returns the same doubles as the original. Unit: the typed boundary of Load(base: const double*) produces double, and Load(base: uint64_t*) read by a FloatAdd spells exactly one reinterpretation.
findings.complexity: O(1) per access.
findings.invariant: The type stated for a rendered expression is the C type that expression has, after removing const and restrict qualifiers only.
findings.risks: Type-punned loads must still reinterpret, and volatile must survive. A pointer declared by DWARF whose pointee disagrees with the machine width must fall back to the machine type and not be trusted.

findings.defect: rv_O0g avg is full of dead XMM lane noise: `__uint128_t XMM0_1; XMM0_1 = (XMM0_1 & ~(...<<64)) | ...` for movsd upper-lane zeroing and loop-carried XMM0 writes that nothing observes. The return is spelled `r2sleigh_float_from_bits_64((uint64_t)XMM0_1)`. rv_O0g sext shows the same Insert noise on RAX.
findings.root_cause: Confirmed. It has the same origin as (a) of the sext finding: there is no Insert transfer, and roots are seeded at the full carrier width. Both halves matter. The Insert transfer alone already makes the loop chain XMM0_2..XMM0_7 unobserved, because XMM0_8 reads only XMM0_7's bytes 8..15, which are the constant-0 lane. Root seeding at 8 bytes is what removes the constant upper-lane write. DeadPhis::find_from (deadphi.rs:384-420) uses the same dependency_closure for elision, so the fix does propagate to r2dec elision. That also means every transfer becomes load-bearing for correctness. A transfer that under-approximates would delete live computation, so the per-op proof harness from the sext finding is mandatory, not optional.

findings.root_cause: I confirm both causes and correct the proposed fix for the first. (a) Leaf types are chosen by the consumer. intern_value types every operand as Integer{Unsigned} whatever its producer, and only BoolNot/And/Or/Xor consumers call intern_boolean_value. The same value therefore gets different leaf types from different consumers, and same_value (which requires equal ty) treats them as different values. The proposer wanted r2ssa to lower bool != to Xor. That would create a second owner of the identity already proven by r2rewrite flag.BOOL_NE_IS_XOR, against the one-owner rule. The fix is to type a leaf by its value's producer. (b) subtraction_flags compares with TermId `==` and never unfolds s or o. Leaves are minted per occurrence, so the match can never succeed in production. The same missing unfold affects ordering_and_equality, EQ_OR_LT_IS_LE and LE_AND_NE_IS_LT: it reads arena.term(equal).kind without unfolding, so a multi-use flag leaf (x86 ZF_1, which also feeds the later jne at 0x1484) blocks the <= fold. The proof harness hides all of this because fresh_leaves interns shared Variable terms. The algorithmic root is that value equality is recomputed on each query by a recursive walk (same_value, which has no memo and costs O(tree size)) and is bypassed by any rule that writes ==.

findings.defect: Cast noise: `return (uint32_t)b + (uint32_t)a;` for int add, and `i = (int32_t)((uint32_t)i + 1);` for i++. A 16-bit multiply on narrow unsigned operands is evaluated in signed int (0xffff*0xffff overflows, which is UB). r2dec also keeps a second literal and linear algebra on the C AST whose casts are transparent and whose operations are not wrapped to the operation width.
findings.root_cause: Mostly confirmed, with corrections. (i) Correct: the typed boundary requires the unsigned machine type for every ring op. Under ISO C with no range proof this is the price of freedom from UB, not noise. (ii) Correct: StridedInterval bounds are unsigned, so a range that straddles 0 goes to top and no-signed-overflow cannot be proven. (iii) Correction: the 'narrow Shl' part of the latent UB is wrong in general. For W ≤ 16 and count < W, (2^W-1)·2^(W-1) < 2^31, so a narrow Shl with an in-range count never overflows int. A narrow Shl is UB only when count ≥ W, which is the shift-admissibility finding. The only narrow ring-op UB is 16-bit Mul: 8-bit Mul (255² < 2^31), and Add/Sub/Neg at W ≤ 16, all fit in int. (iv) Correction to the proposer's test: 0xfffffff0 >> 2 already folds correctly, because UIntLit is positive in i64. The real defects are in literal_to_i64: it looks through every Cast, which drops truncation and signedness, so `(uint32_t)-16 >> 2` folds to -4 and `(uint8_t)0x1ff` to 0x1ff. Add and Mul use checked i64 without wrapping at width_bytes, so `(uint32_t)0xffffffff + 1` becomes 0x100000000. Shr is arithmetic on i64. The algebra runs only on marker-free expressions (implementation.rs:529-536), which narrows but does not remove its reach. A third copy lives at analysis/prepared_semantic/mod.rs:2524.

findings.proposed_fix: (1) Carrier choice per ring node in typed.rs. Bitwise ops use the operands' common declared type (exact in two's complement). Add/Sub/Neg at W < 32 use the declared type (int cannot overflow). Mul at W == 16 requires unsigned int operands, which fixes the only real narrow-UB case; drop the Shl clause, which the shift admissibility covers. Add/Sub/Mul at W ≥ 32 use the declared signed type only where r2ssa proves the mathematical result is in range, and otherwise the unsigned carrier. (2) The range proof needs wrapped intervals (Navas et al., PLDI 2012) with the stride kept, replacing the unsigned-only StridedInterval, plus predicate narrowing on signed compares. The avg guard i <s n with n ≤ INT_MAX gives i ≤ INT_MAX-1 without any relational domain. At O0 this needs ranges over the slot-promoted SSA (MemorySSA equality of the guarded load and the incremented load). This is a domain replacement in r2ssa and must keep the lattice height and the widening at back-edge targets. (3) Alternatively, the declared dialect is GNU C with -fwrapv. That is a policy decision. The output already relies on GCC's implementation-defined unsigned-to-signed conversion and arithmetic right shift. (4) Delete r2dec's C-AST literal and linear algebra (implementation.rs:494-655 and 1285-1310, prepared_semantic:2524). r2rewrite's literal and affine rules are the only owner.

cross_cutting:
Objections across the proposals:
(1) One fact, many renderers. r2dec lowers the same operation in four places: the statement path over SSAOp (implementation.rs op_to_stmt_impl), the machine-expr path (lowering.rs ~700), the term path (lowering.rs ~1030), and subscript_renderer.rs. Each decides types and operator spelling on its own. That is why shift UB has four copies and why the float-load type claim diverged from the access renderer. The real fix is to make op_lower render-only: one typed expression (term or machine) per value, one spelling table that consumes TypedBoundaries' per-node admissibility, and a statement path that only assigns that expression. It is effectively a rewrite of fold/op_lower. Doing it before the shift, float-load and cast fixes saves making each fix four times.
(2) The byte dependency relation is the unifying fact and should be one r2ssa module. The proposer spread it across findings 2, 5, 6 and 9. One dep(op, out_byte) relation should produce backward demand (deadphi, and through it elision), a forward may-unspecified closure, a must-unspecified closure restricted to bijective edges, parameter and result widths, and the ValueRanges treatment of filler. Because DeadPhis uses the same closure for elision, every transfer becomes correctness-critical. It needs a per-op proof harness (flip bytes outside dep(M), check that the output bytes in M are unchanged), not only end-to-end tests.
(3) Soundness direction of narrowing. May-dependence on unspecified inputs can only justify a refusal. It cannot justify narrowing, because over-approximated taint drops real result bytes silently. Narrowing needs must-dependence or consumer corroboration: callers' observed bytes, with the call graph closed.
(4) Ranges have one owner. The proposed term-level interval pass in r2rewrite would be a second range owner. Import r2ssa ValueRanges as leaf facts through the existing declare_leaf_facts channel and reuse the exported StridedInterval transfers.
(5) Value identity should be algorithmic, not audited. Replace the recursive same_value with hash-consed value numbers computed at intern time (O(1) equality), and remove TermId == from the matcher API, so the occurrence-identity bug class cannot come back. Also type leaves by their producer in r2ssa. Do not lower bool != to Xor in r2ssa: that duplicates r2rewrite's proven BOOL_NE_IS_XOR.
(6) IPA-RA is already modelled (CalleePreservedCarriers), and rv_O2 main depends on it: avg's xmm0 result is read only after `call fact`. So refusing CallDefine reads is correct only after those summaries are applied, and the float-result finding's caller evidence goes through fact's summary.
(7) Cross-architecture gaps in the proposals. AArch64 x8 (indirect result) is listed only as clobbered in cc-arm-64.sdb.txt, so an unspecified-at-entry seed would wrongly refuse sret functions. Darwin x18 is reserved. Win64 float args are positional (ms float_args is empty). ARM32 hard-float back-fills. AArch64 SDIV defines INT_MIN/-1 and x/0, while C does not.
(8) Cleanups found along the way: MachineOvershiftBehavior::MaskCount and ::Checked have no producer. The r2dec literal algebra has a third copy in analysis/prepared_semantic. The radare2 cc sdb is the upstream source of r2abi data (crates/r2abi/data/README.md), so any new register class key needs an upstream radare2 PR.
open_questions: Output C dialect: declare GNU C with -fwrapv (plus the GCC implementation-defined conversions and arithmetic right shift the output already relies on) as the product contract, or stay strict ISO C and pay for a wrapped-interval domain in r2ssa so signed carriers are used only where proven? This decides the scope of the cast-discipline finding.

Total spellings: prelude helpers (r2sleigh_shl_32, r2sleigh_rotl_32, r2sleigh_sdiv_32_aarch64) or inline idioms such as `(x << t) | (x >> (-t & 31))`? Helpers are exact and evaluate each argument once. Inline code reads better and compilers recognise rotate idioms.

findings.root_cause: CONFIRMED, with corrections. (1) A loader write is modelled as a bare Range (loader/mod.rs:12-27), and the listing's only memory reader refuses it (records.rs:80-91 word, 74-78 text). (2) CORRECTION to the evidence: loader/macho.rs does NOT 'walk the targets and drop them'. chain() (macho.rs:321-333) reads each word only to extract `next`. The rebase stream never reads the word. The bind stream skips the symbol name (`state.string()`, :416) and the ordinal/addend (:411-415). The chained-fixup import table (imports_offset/symbols_offset of dyld_chained_fixups_header) is never read. The value and bind-target decoders are NEW work, not dropped data. (3) CORRECTION to the math: the proposal's 'value = B+A with B = baddr' is wrong. For ELF RELATIVE the value in link coordinates is A (RELA) or the file word (REL). glibc applies `l_addr + addend`, and l_addr, the load BIAS, is 0 in link coordinates whatever the first PT_LOAD vaddr is. A PIE or .so linked at a nonzero base would be off by baddr under the proposal. Mach-O depends on the pointer format. Classic rebase: value = file word. DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64 (fmt 2) and arm64e non-auth: value = target|high8<<56 (already vmaddr). DYLD_CHAINED_PTR_64_OFFSET (6), arm64e auth and USERLAND: mach-header vmaddr + target. Verified on the fixture: word 0x00100000000003c0 has target 0x3c0, so 0x100000000+0x3c0 = 0x1000003c0, and next = 2 (x4 = 8 bytes). PE: file word. (4) A SECOND READER was missed: native.rs:1735-1760 pointer_table reads table words with program.read and never consults loader_writes, so the decompiler's dispatch reads raw chain encodings on Mach-O and zeros on lld-linked PIE (no --apply-dynamic-relocs). native.rs:2212-2218 text_at also skips the guard that records.rs:74-78 applies. (5) The reference index sources are Line-only (references.rs:68-92,121-137), and axt prints per owner (commands.rs:336-346).

findings.proposed_fix: Keep the proposal's LoaderWrite{place,width,kind,value} list, with these corrections. (a) Coordinate rule per kind, with no global B. ELF RELATIVE/RELR: A or file word. ELF R_*_64/GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT against a definition: Resolved(S+A) only when the definition is NON-PREEMPTIBLE. That holds when the image is the executable (ET_EXEC, DF_1_PIE or PT_INTERP: first in lookup scope), when st_other is HIDDEN/PROTECTED, or under DT_SYMBOLIC/DF_SYMBOLIC. Otherwise record Preemptible{symbol, default:S+A}. IRELATIVE: Resolver(A), whose value is unknown, but A is a stated code pointer and a discovery seed. TLS (DTPMOD/DTPOFF/TPOFF): NotAnAddress. COPY: contents Unknown. MIPS implicit GOT: LocalGot (file word) / GlobalGot(sym). Mach-O: per-format decode as above. Weak binds are Preemptible. BIND_SPECIAL_DYLIB_SELF binds resolve inside the image. (b) Several writes to one place compose in the loader's application order (RELA table order; Mach-O rebase, bind, weak-bind). The stated value is the last write's, and Preemptible if any later write is. (c) One reader, `stated_word(place,width) -> Option<StatedWord>`, replaces raw reads in records.rs word/text, native.rs pointer_table and native.rs text_at. (d) A stated INITIAL value is a reference fact (the image states it), but it is a RUNTIME value, usable for pointer-table callee sets and pdd folding, only if the word is immutable after load: inside PT_GNU_RELRO or a non-W PT_LOAD for ELF; a segment with SG_READ_ONLY or initprot without W for Mach-O. The fixture qualifies (flags 0x10). (e) Listing semantics: add a distinct annotation for 'the loader writes V here' rather than reusing Holds ('this revision's bytes hold V'). State that a patch under a loader write is overwritten at load. (f) The references to emit are decided by relocation-type semantics (address-valued kinds), not by 'value lands in a loaded section'; a one-past-end pointer (&arr[N]) is a real reference. (g) DWARF CU-level DW_TAG_variable (DW_OP_addr + type) is a stated type, but not 'the only proof' in a non-PIE image. r2types use-typing of a global (every load of it flows to a char* parameter) is another. That can follow later. The current pdd `extern char g_msg[]` + `*(uint64_t*)&g_msg` (out/rv_O0g.main.pdd:23-24,113) shows the type gap costs pdd too. (h) axt spelling for a datum source: radare2 prints `(nofunc)` for a source outside any function. Naming the containing object (obj.g_msg) is more informative; decide explicitly.

findings.proposed_fix: Keep the proposal with these corrections. (a) 'DT_* only, sections only for ET_REL' would drop a static non-PIE executable's .rela.iplt: its IRELATIVE entries are applied by start-up code through __rela_iplt_start/__rela_iplt_end, and no DT_ entry covers them. That is exactly what sectioned() exists for (elf.rs:24). The correct rule is identity by RECORD, not by target. Collect every relocation table the dynamic segment names plus every SHF_ALLOC SHT_REL/RELA/RELR section. Key each entry by (table file offset, index), and deduplicate tables that the two routes both reach by their file range. That is one reader and no loss. (b) Mach-O: keep the symbol-pointer section entries as Bind writes (they are real loader writes) and move only S_SYMBOL_STUBS to import_stubs(). On chained-fixup images the bind names must come from the chained imports table (new decoder, see finding 1), because the indirect symbol table may be absent or partial there. (c) The ir `type` column prints the psABI name plus ntype, and a symbol-less entry prints its addend, as proposed.

(2) pdd's literals are harvested with no use evidence at all: native.rs:2237-2254 referenced() takes every nonzero Const- or Ram-space input of any op as an address, and :2102-2107 and :1810-1831 render text_at() for each. findings.proposed_fix: (1) SectionRole from container structure, as proposed. It is sound. (2) String evidence is TYPED USE, not reachability. Any one of these suffices: (a) the container states the bytes are C strings (SHF_MERGE|SHF_STRINGS, S_CSTRING_LITERALS); (b) DWARF types the object as char[]/char*; (c) r2types proves the pointer flows to a parameter declared const char* (printf fmt, strlen, puts) or is read bytewise to a NUL. (3) Delete referenced()'s 'every constant is an address' harvest. pdd literals come from the same evidence set, keyed by the value's proven type, so a Const operand of an arithmetic op is never a literal. (4) iz lists proven strings plus scan candidates in Data/StringLiterals roles, with an evidence column; izz scans every loaded section; bytes the loader writes are never scanned. (5) Escape as radare2 does, and derive the flag identifier from the escaped text. findings.root_cause: r2ssa/indirect.rs:301-334 dispatch_table_read accepts any strided interval with bounds as a table extent. It computes `entries = (last - base)/stride + 1` and materialises `(0..entries).map(..).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()` before checking that the interval lies in mapped memory. At -O0 the selector is spilled: `mov [rbp-4],edi; cmp dword [rbp-4],7; ja; mov eax,[rbp-4]`. The guard constrains the first load, not the reload, so the reach of `0x2018 + 4*zext32(load)` is about 2^32 entries. Deeper origin: the value-range refinement of the guard does not carry through the non-escaping frame slot (no store-to-load forwarding / memory SSA before dispatch analysis). With forwarding, the reload is the same value and the reach is [0,7].

(2) Origin: before the dispatch analysis runs, forward stores to loads for frame slots whose address does not escape. That is the promotion the prepared path already performs, and it must precede dispatch_table_reads. Then the compare's refinement bounds the reloaded selector exactly. Complexity: O(uses of the slot) per slot with the existing def-use.

The only claim for a formed address is Computes, which requires that 'nothing later derives another number from it' (records.rs:254-264). findings.owner_crate: r2ssa (effective-address value ranges: evidence), r2engine (interval references + stabbing query), r2s (axt)
findings.proposed_fix: Claim the ACCESS, not the intermediate. For each load/store/call whose effective address has a bounded strided interval [lo, hi] step s (value ranges already exist per walked body: the Bounds annotation), emit Reference{to: Interval(lo, hi, s), role: Read/Write{width}}. Do this only when the interval lies inside one loaded section, and report the object that starts at lo when one does. A PC-relative formation is always an address of the image (it moves with the image), so the forming instruction also gets Role::Value at its exact value. cross_cutting:
These are objections to the reviewed plan. The evidence citations mostly hold, and I re-read each one. What fails is several of the fixes.

1. Wrong coordinate math in the loader-value model. The plan takes "value = B + A with B = baddr" and ties it to the `i` baddr finding. For ELF, the relocation value in link coordinates is A, or the file word for REL, because the load bias is 0 there. Adding baddr is wrong for any PIE or .so linked at a nonzero base. Mach-O uses the header vmaddr only for offset-form chained pointers; formats 2 and arm64e non-auth already store vmaddr. baddr must stay a presentation fact. I verified this on the fixture: the chained word 0x00100000000003c0 decodes to target 0x3c0 at header 0x100000000, with next = 8 bytes.

2. Soundness gaps in "stated values":
   - Definitions that another library can override (default-visibility symbols in a .so, Mach-O weak binds) are not Resolved.
   - IRELATIVE is a resolver pointer, not a value.
   - TLS relocations are not addresses.
   - Using an initial value as a runtime value (pointer-table callee sets, pdd folding) needs the word to be read-only after loading: PT_GNU_RELRO, a non-writable segment, or Mach-O SG_READ_ONLY. The fixture's __DATA_CONST has flags 0x10, so it qualifies; writable .data does not.
   - Emitting references by "value lands in a loaded section" is a location heuristic. It drops one-past-end pointers. The relocation type should decide instead.

3. Two memory readers the plan did not name. native.rs:1741 (pointer_table) and native.rs:2212 (text_at) read raw file bytes whether or not the loader writes them, while records.rs refuses those bytes. That is the "one fact, one owner" violation behind decompiler table reads of raw chain encodings, and of zeros on lld-linked binaries.

4. One body per function is not what the survey has. Switch arms appear only in prepare's second walk (native.rs:736-760). Building afl, function_at, the reference index and pdf XREF lines from survey walks, as the afl and function_at fixes propose, would bake in the disagreement. Table resolution has to move into the survey fixpoint.

5. A crash was missed. afi, pdf and pdd on any -O0 jump-table function run out of memory in r2ssa indirect.rs:319-334, from an unbounded strided reach. The stored out/rv_O0g.classify.pdd is the crash backtrace, so part of the planned test matrix cannot run until this is fixed.

6. Reachability is not string evidence. The iz fix would still name the CSWTCH.12 u32 table "\n", which pdd already renders today. It would also leave native.rs referenced(), which treats every immediate as an address, as the real source of pdd literals. Strings need typed-use evidence from r2types, or a container statement. Widening text_in before that makes pdd worse.

7. The NameDb alias order would pick the wrong name. At 0x4020 it keeps .data's one-past-end marker (__TMC_END__) over the object that occupies the byte (completed.0). Order by occupancy first, which needs Symbol.section from r2image.

8. Name-first code is wider than the plan says:
   - is_generated_function_name treats Mach-O `_add`/`_face` and any `sub_*`/`loc.*` symbol as generated, and r2ssa then drops the real name.
   - normalize_callee_name keys `sub_add` as address 0xadd.
   - is_low_quality_stack_name treats a real DWARF local named `stack_*`, `local_*` or `arg_*` as a placeholder.
   - Stub sections are chosen by name (naming.rs:435).
   - stack_m/p names are spelled in three r2dec places in two coordinate systems, plus r2s.
   Changing the unnamed spelling to fcn.%08x without deleting these parsers keeps identity collisions.

9. The AArch64 `lsl ` fault is in the Sleigh spec, AARCH64instructions.sinc:2196 and :2239-2244, in the user-owned sleigh-config fork. It should be fixed there, with an upstream Ghidra PR, not in r2sleigh-lift text rewriting.

10. The duplicated container types (engine source.rs, r2image, session.rs) are how facts get narrowed away. Unify them first, or each new fact costs three edits and invites another silent loss.

11. The radare2 source lines the plan cites (cbin.c, canal.c, disasm.c, bfile.c, elf.c, mach0.c, cmd_quit.inc.c) could not be checked: no radare2 source or binary is available here. The behaviours I relied on (afl columns, fcn.%08x, (nofunc) in axt, ie listing init/fini) should be checked against a live r2 before goldens are fixed.

Recommended order:
   - (0) the dispatch OOM crash fix, and the unified container types;
   - (1) r2image: one relocation-record reader, LoaderWrite with per-format values and binds, SectionRole, segment immutability, Symbol bind/visibility/section, baddr;
   - (2) one stated_word reader used by the listing, dispatch tables and literals;
   - (3) survey fixpoint with dispatch resolution, keeping block extents; function_at; interval references;
   - (4) typed names (Stated/Discovered), deleting the spellers and the name parsers;
   - (5) typed-use string evidence in r2types, with iz/izz;
   - (6) afv roles from entity.source_slot;
   - (7) r2s rendering (pdf header, columns, escaping, prefix, exit codes).
open_questions: Stated loader values in decompilation: may pdd and the indirect-call resolver use a stated word as the runtime value only when it is read-only after load (PT_GNU_RELRO, non-writable segment, Mach-O SG_READ_ONLY), with writable-.data initial values limited to references (axt/ir)? That is the sound split. Or should stated values stay out of decompilation entirely?

Preemptible definitions: in a shared library, should a GLOB_DAT/R_64 against a default-visibility defined symbol render as the local definition with a visible 'may be interposed' residual, or as an import-like unknown?

iz semantics: str.* flags and pdd literals only from typed-use evidence or container statements, with iz listing those plus scan candidates marked by an evidence column and izz scanning everything? Or should iz copy radare2's name-based data-section scan with its fixed minimum length of 4?
Shared tails: when function_at finds k>1 owners, refuse and list the owners (recommended), or pick the lowest entry as radare2 effectively does?

Unnamed spelling: switch everything to fcn.%08x / fcn_%08x (every fcn_{x} golden changes)? And should a function handed to __libc_start_main arg 0, whose declaration names it `main`, take that declared name (a statement from the ABI declaration) or stay fcn.X with only the type flowing?
axt for a data source: radare2 prints `(nofunc)` for a source outside any function. Should r2s match it, or name the containing object (obj.g_msg), which says more?
afl layout: radare2's exact headerless `addr nbbs size name`, with the confidence column moved to a verbose afl variant?

-O0 main: DWARF locals (v, a, b, c, d, buf, r) reach neither afv nor pdd, and struct layouts are not read from DWARF (debug.rs spells types as strings only). Is that in scope for this cluster or the types cluster?
Exit status: follow radare2 (q -> 0, q N -> N) or keep 'any failed statement -> 1'? Today a clean `q` also exits 1.

findings.defect: PR #26768 'Keep the Thumb bit off data symbols in ARM ELF'. It is OPEN and mergeable (mergeable_state=clean, base 39b18895). CI is green on head 7b459eca: 49 checks, 25 success and 24 skipped (the skipped ones are gated jobs), none failing. There are 2 UNRESOLVED review threads, both from trufae on 2026-09-19: (a) elf.c:5152 'Remove all those comments'; (b) elf.c:5157 'Replace the is_code variable with an is_code function that takes sym and does its thing in a separate code block for readability. 1 line comment...'. trufae then posted 'Ping' on 2026-09-21 and has had no reply. There are also two correctness gaps the reviewer did not raise: (1) STT_GNU_IFUNC is a code symbol, and on ARM a Thumb IFUNC resolver carries bit 0. r2 reports its type as R_BIN_TYPE_LOOS_STR, and the PR's FUNC/LOPROC test excludes that, so Thumb IFUNCs regress to an odd address with bits=32. (2) A sibling site holds the same fact: Elf_(get_bits) counts `symbol->offset & 1` over every symbol that is not a mapping symbol, OBJECTs included, and treats it as Thumb evidence. So in a binary without $a/$t mapping symbols, an odd-addressed data object still flips the whole binary to bits=16.
findings.root_cause: The ARM AAELF rule is that bit 0 of st_value selects the ISA only for code symbols (STT_FUNC, STT_ARM_TFUNC=STT_LOPROC, STT_GNU_IFUNC). radare2 applied that rule to every symbol type, in two places that do not share a predicate. The PR fixes one of the two places and misses one of the three code types.

It is OPEN, mergeable (clean) and CI green on head 2774ebf8, with no inline threads. trufae posted one COMMENTED review (2026-09-21 00:09) and it has not been answered. It asks for 9 things: (1) refactor so LLDB reuses the GDB register-read path instead of gdbr_read_registers_lldb's parallel buffer sizing, per-register loop, thread-suffix, packet/ack handling and hex unpacking; (2) one stop-reply register parser instead of gdbr_cache_lldb_stop_registers duplicating handle_lldb_read_reg; (3) gdbr_read_process_info is called twice on a successful attach; (4) qProcessInfo is sent unconditionally on every gdbserver connect and should be gated on LLDB or an advertised capability; (5) gdbr_connect_lldb hardcodes g=false instead of probing it; (6) strdup/free of every stop packet in gdbr_stop_reason, gdbr_attach and send_vcont should become one path in stop-reply handling; (7) the buffer growth `while (newsize <= len) newsize *= 2` can wrap size_t from remote input, and data_max is narrower than size_t; (8) the Darwin CPU-type map in core.c duplicates arch knowledge and belongs in a reusable place or should use target.xml; (9) protocol-level regression tests: normal gdbserver still uses g, LLDB with and without g, pN fallback, stop reply with registers, thread suffix on/off, bit-sized offsets, oversized response, attach T reply. Its one thread is resolved, but the formal CHANGES_REQUESTED review of 2026-09-05 is still on record. trufae's 2026-09-22 00:03 comment says no correctness blocker and asks for: a nit in r_anal_extract_rarg, where the else branch recomputes is_reg_in_src/r_anal_cc_location_uses and should reuse in_src||in_dst; a PR description update (it still says the fp guard 'goes away', describes an arm64 regression, and asks steering questions); and the squash subject 'Cache calling-convention argument locations per function'. Deeper issue I found: the cache key is wrong. ArgSeqCache is keyed on (fcn pointer, fcn->callconv, cc_generation), but its content (32 r_anal_cc_argloc results plus r_anal_cc_max_arg) depends only on (callconv, cc_generation). Keying on fcn re-resolves all 32 slots every time analysis moves between two functions with the same convention, which is nearly always during aaa. It also compares a possibly freed-and-reused pointer (harmless only because the content does not depend on fcn).
findings.root_cause: The invariant is 'argument locations are a property of the convention', but the cache key encodes 'per function'. The else-branch recompute is left over from before in_src/in_dst were computed at the top of the loop.

PR diff var.c: argseq_of fills loc[i] from r_anal_cc_argloc(anal, fcn->callconv, i, 0, 0) and max_arg from r_anal_cc_max_arg(anal, fcn->callconv): no fcn dependence

findings.proposed_fix: Key the cache on (callconv constpool pointer, cc_generation) and drop the fcn field. Replace the else branch with `if (!partial) reg_set[slot] = 2;`. Rewrite the PR description to describe the current implementation, and use trufae's subject line. Ask for re-review so the CHANGES_REQUESTED state clears. findings.defect: PR #25942 'Optimize /as syscall search candidate discovery'. It is OPEN, mergeable (clean), CI green on head 54b79883 (rebased 2026-09-19). Two CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews (2026-05-12 'fix those and im mainly interested for perf on arm32/arm64'; 2026-06-05) are still on record. All 14 inline threads are marked resolved/outdated, but two structural asks are only partly met: 'use RSearch chunked blocks and honor the alignment' (the head now uses r_search keywords with masks, so this is met) and 'is it really necessary to have arch-specific collectors... find an aligned pattern in a generic way once' (the head still hardcodes per-arch byte/mask tables in core, in syscall_candidate_search_init X86/ARM64/ARM32/THUMB). The author's question of 2026-09-19 is unanswered: libflutter.so (arm32) goes from 8 to 34 hits and gets slower; 'is the wider coverage intended?' The answer is NO. The 26 extra hits are false positives from two defects that master hides by accident: (1) the candidate domain is the IO maps (param->boundaries -> r_io_map_begin/end), which include .rel.dyn inside the R-X PT_LOAD; (2) when the syscall-number register is unknown, the code falls back to `scNumber = aop.val` (the svc immediate). On ARM EABI the number is in r7 and the immediate is 0; only OABI encodes 0x900000+nr. So data words `svc 0xc` and `svc 0x10` become chdir(12) and lchown(16), which is exactly what the author reports. Master rejects them only because its linear local_state carries garbage constants through data.
findings.root_cause: The syscall number is taken from an encoding field that does not carry it under the target ABI, and code is identified by mapping permission rather than section type.
evidence: issue comment 5744823614 (author): libflutter base 8 hits in .text, branch 34, extras e.g. `0x0000bfe4 chdir`, `0x00023914 lchown` in .rel.dyn, decoding as svc 0xc / svc 0x10
master libr/core/cmd_scsearch.inc.c:866-868 domain = param->boundaries maps; ~:910-918 `scNumber = aop.val` fallback; ~:921-923 `r_syscall_get (..., scVector, -1)` for non-x86
PR head cmd_scsearch.inc.c ~1003-1044 per-arch keyword tables; ~1050 syscall_collect_candidates over the same boundaries
review threads PRRT_kwDOAEpMrs6HTHWL ('arch-specific collectors... spaghetti'), PRRT_kwDOAEpMrs6HTGbV ('use rarchinfo')
findings.owner_crate: radare2: libr/core/cmd_scsearch.inc.c (policy); libr/arch plugins (encodings/alignment via RArchInfo)
findings.proposed_fix: Reply with the diagnosis. Make the number resolution ABI-correct: take the number from the syscall register (r7 on ARM EABI, eax/rax on x86 syscall) as proven by the CFG/transfer. Use the immediate only where the ABI puts the number there (ARM OABI: imm-0x900000; x86 `int` gives the vector, not the number). Otherwise refuse the hit. Restrict candidates to executable sections (SHF_EXECINSTR) intersected with search.in boundaries when section headers exist, falling back to maps only without sections. For the reviewer, move the pattern knowledge behind the arch plugin (RArchInfo/plugin-provided syscall encodings plus code alignment) so core runs one generic aligned masked scan. Re-measure arm32 and arm64.
findings.test: An r2r case on bins/elf/libflutter.so (or a small arm32 fixture with a relocation table containing 0x0f00000c words): `/as~chdir` must print nothing outside .text, and `/asq` must list only the 8 .text hits. Plus a crafted ARM EABI blob `mov r7, #12; svc #0` that must resolve chdir, and an `svc #0xc` with unknown r7 that must NOT resolve.
findings.complexity: One O(N) masked scan plus O(C) decodes over candidates C, instead of O(N) decodes
findings.risks: The OABI-vs-EABI choice must come from ELF e_flags (EF_ARM_EABI_MASK). Existing test expectations that rely on immediate-derived numbers may change.
